Teaching study: the risk matrix is an example; alarm limits and trips are read from the simulator.

1

Part 1

How is the P&ID divided and questioned?

Part 1 · the plan

A fixed loop, run until nothing is left

  1. The examination loopnode, intent, parameter, guide word
  2. Ten nodesone design intent each
  3. Guide wordseleven words, eleven parameters
  4. Coverage87 deviations recorded

Step 1 · IEC 61882

Every guide word meets every parameter of every node

Severity is judged without safeguards; likelihood with them. Every deviation is written down, even when nothing is found: full recording.

Step 2 · interactive · nodes

Where does one design intent end and the next begin?

N10 has no equipment: start-up, purge and light-off are where fired heaters explode.

Step 3 · interactive · guide words

What does each guide word ask of the design?

Only physically meaningful pairs are recorded: there is no "reverse temperature".

Step 4 · interactive · coverage check

Did any node skip a guide word?

Click a cell. The time words (EARLY, LATE, BEFORE, AFTER) find deviations only in the procedures node N10.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • A node is a stretch of plant with one design intent; V-1 has ten.
  • Guide word × parameter gives a deviation; only meaningful pairs are kept.
  • The coverage table shows that no combination was skipped.

One row, read from left to right

  1. One worksheet rowdeviation to recommendation
  2. The 87 rows on the matrixnine High, none Very high
  3. Safeguards that share a sensorwhy High rows go to LOPA

Step 1 · interactive · worksheet

Read one row from deviation to recommendation

Step 2 · interactive · 5 × 5 matrix

Where do the 87 deviations land?

Node

High (10–16) is not tolerable as is: a recommendation is required, and a LOPA / SIL review.

Step 3 · independence

An alarm on the same transmitter as the loop is not a second layer

RowSafeguard listedWeaknessRecommendation
N4-01FSL-105A tripuses FT-105A, the control transmitterR07 independent sensors
N9-01PIC-102 high alarma PIC-102 transmitter fault is one of the causesR19 independent high-high

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • A row reads deviation, causes, consequences, safeguards, S × L, recommendation.
  • 87 rows: 9 High, 75 Medium, 3 Low.
  • A safeguard counts only if it is independent of the cause.
3

Part 3

What does the team recommend, and what does the simulator add?

Part 3 · the plan

A recommendation is closed, not just written

  1. The recommendation register29 actions, each with a discipline
  2. Dynamic checkthe deviation run on a copy of the model
  3. Close-outowner, LOPA, MOC, revalidation

Step 1 · interactive · register

Which recommendations address the highest risk?

Discipline

Step 2 · interactive · 30 min on a copy of the model

How long does the operator have before the trip?

No operator action, every controller, alarm and trip active. The running simulator is never touched.

Step 3 · follow-up

The study is finished when every action is closed

StepWhat is done
Owner and dateOPEN → RESPONDED → CLOSED, accepted by the HAZOP leader
LOPAthe 9 High rows and every row relying on a trip: L1–L7, then SIL and SRS
MOCany change to P&ID, set points, trips or procedures re-opens the touched nodes
Revalidationat least every five years, after a major change or an incident
Trainingrun the dynamic checks with operators on this OTS (R25)

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • 29 recommendations; the High ones target sensors, trips and procedures.
  • The model shows the time between the first alarm and the trip.
  • A trip limits damage; it may not prevent it (pass A skin 840 °C before the trip).

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Choose nodes by design intent, then apply every guide word.

2

Record every deviation, even when nothing is found.

3

Credit a safeguard only if it is independent of the cause.

4

Test the worst deviations on the model before trusting the trip.
